description:
FILED s470bs (Opus), found while taking the companion baseline for the
filetest/stat family.  PRE-EXISTING (identical on the s470bs base 027ba9c).

MEASURED: `tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1 op/stat.t`

    op/stat.t   P: 108/3   C: 0/0   DIFF
    aborted-forms:1: Undefined subroutine &main::is_linux_container called

The file's line 54 is a FILE-LEVEL call:

    my $Is_linux_container = is_linux_container();

and the sub is defined in perl's own t/test.pl (line 2056), which op/stat.t
`require`s from a BEGIN block.  So the sub exists by the time the call runs in
perl, and does not in PCL.

WHAT MAKES IT INTERESTING: the definition sits immediately after a line that
closes a file-spanning closure â

    } # End closure

    # Orphaned Docker or Linux containers â¦
    sub is_linux_container { â¦ }

    1;

â i.e. it is the LAST sub in the file, after a `}` at column 0 that ends a
`{ â¦ }` block wrapping most of test.pl.  The obvious suspicions are (a) the
sub is dropped/not defined when it follows that block, or (b) it is defined in
the wrong package.  NEITHER IS MEASURED YET.

THE CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, not taken here (this file was outside
the s470bs brief): transpile perl's t/test.pl alone
(`./pl2cl <perl-suite-t>/test.pl | grep -n 'is-linux-container'`) and see
whether a `(p-sub pl-is-linux-container â¦)` form is emitted at all, and in
which package.  If it is emitted, the question is the LOAD, not the parse.

WORTH: 108 perl rows in a file that currently contributes NOTHING, plus
whatever else in the companion depends on the tail of t/test.pl.
subject: t/op/stat.t produces ZERO PCL rows (perl 108/3): "Undefined subroutine &main::is_linux_container called" â a sub defined at the END of perl's own t/test.pl, after its `} # End closure` line.
